args: Assess an UPRIGHT pinch of the TWO PHYSICAL SHORT END WALLS, closing along the long axis, NOT the rejected long-side strips or near-horizontal routes. Request t0..t3 at the supplied SAME physical IDs; declare landmark_identity. Request c0..c2 on noncollinear counter. Request a0,a1 as upper/lower samples on one SHORT END wall and b0,b1 on the OPPOSITE end, with complementary views/radius 1 as needed. Occluded faces are unknown. Give four top-edge pixels in one camera, ordered A-strip-end1,A-strip-end2,B-strip-end2,B-strip-end1, delimiting aligned end-contact strips about 25 mm wide. No whole perimeter. Request s0..s3: fresh top interiors spanning both directions; declare sN_surface individually. These support the plane, not new t IDs. Upright orientation alone does not resolve the old height deficit; an infeasible interval prevents approach. Note any visible presentation alternative without authorizing it. Use a DIFFERENT camera or different depth-valid surface samples to replace failed measurements; do not repeat the same mixed-depth pixels.

historical_failure.guard_accounting: Counter bound includes guard plus pose tolerance plus the original 3 mm clearance. Overlap includes guard plus pose tolerance above 5 mm and never lowers the rejected candidate's 7 mm nominal threshold. Top floor uses the lowest measured upper corner, not the higher center. The interval is for the planned orientation; actual finger orientation and margins are rechecked before closure.
historical_failure.candidate_change: Choose a lower height inside a measured feasible interval with a tighter pose deadband, not a lowered clearance or overlap threshold.
reference_top_ids: t0: inner curl of the large initial capital C in the printed word Cream, toward the exposed short end.
t1: inner curl of the large initial capital C in the printed word Cheese, below Cream in this view.
t2: initial F of the smaller printed Fresh Taste line, left of the large lettering in this view.
t3: terminal e of the smaller printed Fresh Taste line, toward the inward end of that line.

excluded_route.family: near-horizontal long-side entry at +/-88 and +/-90 degrees
excluded_route.established_obstruction: Palm intersects counter during descent; high alignment alone was clear.

result.explanation: Assessment and measurement only; no approach or closure is authorized. The current views show the cream-cheese package flat on the counter and an empty open hand. The printed landmarks match the supplied physical IDs. Earlier frames are supplied as records, not images, so an independent earlier-image comparison is unavailable. A is the short end at the upper wrist-image boundary and lower agentview boundary. Its vertical wall is visible in agentview. Opposite B's vertical wall is hidden by the package in both views: b0/b1 and a B-wall region are unavailable. The visible long-side wall is not a substitute. This is unobserved contact geometry, not an observed external obstruction or current robot self-occlusion. Visible short-end top edges support a local strip model, but do not establish two usable opposed end-wall contacts. Upright orientation alone does not repair the height deficit. Every supplied interval fails the minimum-width requirement, including the positive 0.106 mm interval that is narrower than 0.200 mm. Approach remains blocked pending a measured feasible interval and adequate contact evidence. The exposed broad top is a possible surface for separately assessing a presentation change; no raised or overhanging end is visible and no such action is authorized. The rejected near-horizontal routes remain excluded.

parameters.notes: A is upper in wrist view; B is lower. Edge order is A-strip-end1,A-strip-end2,B-strip-end2,B-strip-end1. New top-side lip pixels sit just inside the boundaries to reduce mixed depth; transverse spans are about 25 mm, subject to depth verification. These are short-end strips, not a perimeter. t IDs retain their printed features. New s/c/a samples replace previous sample locations; depth validity still needs checking. b0/b1 are unavailable through object occlusion. Continue permits assessment only, not approach.
